description:
## Problem
On DuckDB, "sorting" is two things:
- an ART index (`idx_<t>_sort`), visible in `duckdb_indexes()`;
- a CTAS or FK-safe in-place rewrite that physically orders rows. It has no catalog footprint.

The ledger records the index. It never records a *successful* rewrite: `benchbox/platforms/base/sorted_ingestion.py:211-320` records only skips (as dropped intents) and failures. `corroborate()` can therefore only check the index, which is a proxy: an index can exist even when the data was never sorted. MotherDuck sorts without creating any index.

## Options
- **(A) Recommended.**
  - Record a successful rewrite as an executed `post_load` statement with `mechanism="sorted_ingestion"`.
  - Classify it as a new non-blocking verdict class `attested`. It is shown in the receipt and never counted as corroboration.
  - Index intents stay catalog-verified.
  - A requested sort with no executed rewrite becomes a dropped intent through the post-load reconciliation, and it blocks.
- **(B) Strict.** Sort intents stay unverifiable without catalog evidence, so DuckDB sorting can never reach `applied_verified`.
- **(C) Rejected.** A bounded data probe of row order would violate the invariant that introspection never measurably slows a run.

## Must decide
- The verdict name and its receipt JSON shape, plus the Explorer label.
- Exactly what `applied_verified` means once `attested` exists.
- Whether a platform with *only* attested evidence (MotherDuck, which has no index) may ever reach `applied_verified`.

## Guardrails
- The decision must not widen what can corroborate. `attested` must never satisfy a catalog-verifiable intent.
- `corroborate()` stays configuration-free (plan review F2). The "requested but not executed" rule lives in the reconciliation.

## Gate protocol
- This is a decision record, not an implementation.
- Implementation items that list this gate in `needs` must not start until it is done.
- The decision owner is the maintainer.
- Record the outcome as a dated ADR addendum (addenda only; do not rewrite recorded decisions) and paste the decision into this item's context before finishing.
